decisions.claim: B is a customer being asked to order food at a restaurant
decisions.reason: The phrase 'May I take your order now?' presupposes B is a customer at a restaurant being offered the opportunity to order. This is a well-grounded inference from the standard restaurant script presupposition.

decisions.claim: B has a salad (or is ordering a salad)
decisions.reason: 'Do you want some salad dressing?' presupposes B has or is getting a salad, since salad dressing is specifically associated with salads. This is a necessary inference from the utterance.
decisions.counterexample: B could be ordering another dish that takes dressing, but the strong default presupposition is a salad.

decisions.claim: B is a customer at a restaurant
decisions.reason: c3 ('B is a customer at a restaurant') is a less specific subset of c1 ('B is a customer being asked to order food at a restaurant'). Both derive from the same evidence and refer to the same property; c1 is the more accurate canonical form.

decisions.claim: B has ordered or is ordering a salad
decisions.reason: c4 ('B has ordered or is ordering a salad') is bidirectionally equivalent to c2 ('B has a salad or is ordering a salad'). Both derive from the same presupposition in turn 3 and express the same claim at the same granularity.
